Municipal Millionaire

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Connected and milking the municipality - how does Khotso Khasu get away with it?

Summary:
It's the kind of scandal that would rock most governments - see forced resignations and heads rolling. but in SA it's swept under the carpet. Even though government assures us they are committed to service delivery - how can they let something like this slide? 46 million missing from the Vryburg municipality, and the corrupt company director appointed to a top position in COPTA? How on earth is this possible? Where is the accountability and why was there no proper vetting?


And what is the bigger picture here? Why does this keep happening and why is corruption not rooted out?


Further information:
South Africa has been dubbed the protest capital of the world, with estimates of around 30 protests a day around the country and 3000 in the first 90 days of the year involving more than a million people. Many of these protests revolve around service delivery and essential services.

Couple this reality with the Auditor General’s report that shows that in the last financial year wasteful, irregular and unaccounted for expenditure in municipalities amounts to 41 billion rand. It’s little wonder people aren’t getting services.

Earlier this year Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa declared that government would not tolerate corruption and would throw the book at perpetrators. The book or cash one has to ask when you look at one of the most blatant examples of siphoning off of municipal funds meant for helping the poor in Vryburg. Khasu Engineering Services were commissioned to build 3500 houses and were paid the full 86 million rand contract price. Only four of the houses were built and according to a cash flow analysis done by a forensic accountant for the SIU millions of rands were moved through 167 accounts during the first year of the contract to friends, relatives and even the head of the Northern Cape Health department Gugu Matloapane who received a million rand. She is a business associate of Frank Khotso Khasu who owns Khasu engineering.

This isn’t the first time that Khasu’s name has come up controversially in big construction projects. In Bloemhof he was given a multi million rand water construction project a few years prior to the Vryburg housing contract and also didn’t deliver. (I am trying to track down the details of the project to see who will talk)

And now despite the fact that he’s taken millions in Vryburg and there is very little to show for it – he’s been rewarded with a top job in the Department of Co-operative Governance and Traditional Affairs and I hear (still trying to confirm) he’s secured another housing contract for tens of millions from government – this time to build houses in Upington for 32 battalion veterans.

All this while the SIU has concluded what they call a cut and dried case with absolute proof that he took the money and never honoured the contract. In fact the four houses that he built were so badly constructed that they were condemned and pulled down.

Why was this man not vetted before getting a top government job? Why 4 years after the SIU report surfaced has no action been taken? Those millions were meant to enhance the lives of the poor – it’s a crime against humanity and so far the Hawks and the NPA have not concluded their investigations. Delaying tactics? We need answers.

BTW when I spoke to Paul Ramaloko about this yesterday he wasn’t sure of the status of the investigation but chuckled and said if you’re looking into this that guy will get fired.

We plan to go to Bloemhof where we have a municipal insider, angry residents who were meant to get houses that never materialized and challenge the municipal manager on what’s being done to get the missing millions back and deliver on the promises to the townsfolk.

Working on getting more info regarding the botched Bloemhof water contract – it’s an hour from Vryburg so we could go there and add that to the story. Pretty sure we can find people to talk. Will also follow up on the 32 Battalion contract.

Then back in Jozi we’ll speak to the SIU whistleblower Anton Kriel he’s a forensic accountant. We’ll also ask for interviews from Pravin Gorhan of COPTA, Hawks, SALGA and the NPA and then of course try to track down Khasu himself for an interview.

Might be worth having an interview with a Paul Hoffman (Centre for Accountability) of Corruption Watch as an objective commentator.

Press Release:


Municipal Millions
Deserted foundations, broken pipes and condemned half-built houses – it’s a right royal mess that’s cost the North West province over R100-million to sort out. Have municipal tenders become nothing more than a get-rich quick scheme for politically connected entrepreneurs? Carte Blanche investigates allegations of tender irregularities, kickbacks and large-scale corruption


Script:


Municipal Millionaire

MM –his predecessor….pick up the pieces….4 years ago… VO:
Deserted foundations stand among weeds in the veld, a short distance away are lone sewerage pipes and rows of badly built houses on the outskirts of the North West town of Vryburg. It’s the handiwork of this man Frank Khotso Khasu, an MK veteran and former head honcho in the provincial department of housing. After pocketing millions he’s abandoned the site in 2009 which offered hope of owning a home to thousands of the town’s poor.

Link
The reality is that the stories just get more and more desperate, it doesn’t matter who you speak to, just on this street alone, the stories are all sad, but they all speak of broken promises.

VO: 5”
Elsie Molefe has been waiting for aouse for 15 years.

Dineo Molefe:
She says it is very painful for her to feel like that.

VO: 8”
Once inside it was hard to believe that the family of 7 is able to sleep in these cramped quarters.

Devi:
So some of the children sleep here on the floor too? And your bathroom? There’s no bathroom?

Elsie:
No bathroom here.

VO: 4”
Next door residents were equally keen to vent their anger.

24:20
17 years I’ve been renting here in this location, but I don’t get a house.


VO: 7”
Some of them showed us documents proving they had been on top of the list for 6 years. Others had beeiven numbers for houses but as the years wore on the houses never materialized.


26:55
When the election comes they are looking for us very high and low, they are going to knock on our houses, but when there is job they don’t come to us, when there is houses like this they don’t come to us.

VO: 7”
Across the road retired and disabled Reginald says he dreams of a home to call his own before he dies.

Devi:
Why is it taking so long?

Reginald:
.Don’t know….don’t know.

VO: 22”
If Frank Khasu had honoured the contract maybe Reginald would be in a house now. Local DA councilor Louwna Pretorius has been trying to get answers for the townsfolk.

Louwna:
Only 4 was really completed and it was also not completed sufficient according to building restrictions.

Devi:
How much did Khasu engineers receive?

Louwna:
On that stage they had received 86 million.

VO:
And only a tenth of project’s houses were in various stages of completion.

Louwna:
The building inspector showed very clear that the foundations got problems, the walls got problems, I even tried to open one of the doors and it fell out!

VO:
Municipal manager – Modisenyane Segapo, who has been left to pick up the pieces, says they had no choice but to terminate Khasu’s contract.

MM:
This was extraordinarily high the number of houses that did not pass the test, this was not your normal, there seemed to be big problems structurally with some of the houses.

VO
We spoke to a contractor brought in to run tests and rectify the shoddy construction – he says the foundations weren’t sound.

Naas:
We tested it and the quality of the concrete, the minimum wasn’t…wasn’t up series of trials or the compression strength wasn’t up to standard. And also the concrete thickness in the areas specified by the engineers wasn’t up to standard.

VO: 4”
Naas says anything you build on top of that structure is unsafe.

Naas:
It wasn’t feasible to fix it, the easiest, most cost effective way was to demolish it.

VO: 9”
The houses have been condemned and squatters have since moved in - despite the fact that the services Khasu was meant to build are non-existent.

Louwna:
They are not completed, there is no electricity, no sewerage lines, there is no water in these houses.

VO: 9”
What was meant to be a municipal asset is now a liability. SIU whistleblower and forensic account with 20 years experience Anton Kriel has been following the money.

Anton:
86 million was paid – there is only 20 million on the ground, so we are basically looking at 60 million – where has that money gone and that is what they wanted to know and that is why they got me involved.

VO: 14
Anton’s job has been to analyse Khasu Engineering’s business account and Khotso Khasu’s two personal accounts. He says the business started with a balance of R123
Anton:
When the first Naledi funds came in at the end of June and you can clearly see then there was a lifestyle beyond anything else…

VO: 14”
Khasu bought a farm for 4.3 million, a 7 series black BMW for 1,3 million, did a kitchen revamp for 45 000, bought high end furniture from Bakos Brothers for 150k and paid for this house in Vryburg with a price tag of just over 800k.

Anton:
On the 1st of Julythere was a payment of a million rand to his wife – we are still tracing that account…
VO: 8”
Then in April 2009 he paid half a million rand into his son Sibusiso’s account who splashed out in Sandton city on Louis Vuiton bags to the value of R5000.

Anton:
It’s a life of luxury and you think this money should have gone for housing, for poor people.

VO: 7”
It was a case of easy come, easy go – Khasu we discovered never tendered for the project either.

MM:
There doesn’t seem to be any indication that the municipality went out on tender. It seems that council made a resolution to let Khasu Engineering implement the project - this is very strange because councilors and council as a whole is not allowed to take part in the procurement process.

Devi:
Have you been able to establish why they even passed this motion?

MM:
The community were demanding that houses be issued, this sort of created an emergency.

VO:
Looking at the financials it seems a greasing of palms of a previous Naledi municipal official may have helped to seal the deal.

Devi:
R350 000 was paid to this man – for what?

Anton: 6”
Again, to me this is possibly corruption and again it needs to be investigated further.

VO: 15”
Municipal insider Sigrit, who served on the housing portfolio committee, believes Khasu may have been shielded by the mayor at the time – Dr Ruth Mompati.

Sigrit:
Very close friends, political friends, sort of like he was a son to her.

VO: Dr Mompati told us the orders came from the provincial head office.

Dr Mompati:

We get informed that he had been given that contract. We had nothing to do with it. I didn’t even know he knew anything about building.


He says the council at the time was used… VO: 3”
The new municipal manager believes the Naledi council was used.

MM:
It would seem to me that the Department wanted this done but they just wouldn’t be the ones doing it. So they went to a municipality that had no proper governance and so on, because Naledi was receiving disclaimers time and time again, so they dumped the problem on Naledi...that’s my view.

VO: 8”
All our attempts to get comment from the Human Settlements dept in the North West were ignored.

Devi link
Khasu engineering’s botch up is not limited to just Vryburg, a few other towns in the Northwest province have also suffered as a result of his handiwork or lack thereof…

VO: 17”
Just prior to the housing contract Khasu also secured two other sanitation contracts in neighbouring Bloemhof and Christiana in the Northwest – to a value of 41 million rand. Civil engineer Lennert van Rooyen was called in to rescue the situation and sort out the mess Khasu left behind.

Lennert:
Very bad/ To the extent that 72% of the lines installed had to be replaced.

VO: 9
He says the sewer systems were completely dysfunctional, presented a serious health hazard and cost 20 million rand to fix.

Lennert:
In layman’s terms the lines were incorrectly designed and installed – a sewer cannot run upstream.

VO: 3”
Sigrit says in Bloemhof like Vryburg Khasu didn’t take responsibility.

Sigrit:
After the inspection the portfolio called him to meetings. He didn’t turn up for one meeting, I believe he always send people to represent him, and they could never get the facts from them.

VO: 16”
He avoided our phone calls and we couldn’t track him down to his registered address in Vryburg or his signature unfinished house in Johannesburg’s upmarket suburb of Houghton. But when the Naledi municipality municipal manager called he explained his evasive behavior.

MM:
He’s taken a decision 6 years ag0 when this thing first came onto the media that he is not going to do any media interviews.

VO: 11
Khasu’s managed to escape the net so far and even scored a Chief Director job at the Department of Co-operative governance and traditional affairs – earning him a minimum salary of nearly a million rand a year.
In the coming months he’ll have some explaining to do in court – next week – the District Municipality are taking him to court for the failed Bloemhof and Christiana projects.

Lennert:
They’ve ordered attorneys to issue a summons, that was served on Khasu, they have launched an application for default judgement in the high court, and we are to tesify in the high court next week on the 19th in fact.

VO: 17
We’ve also established that he wasn’t registered with the Construction Industry Development Board meant to regulate infrastructure delivery and he could face a fine of 8 million. Yet astonishingly Khasu is pursuing more money for the botched housing project from the Naledi municipality on appeal.

MM:
He is in the high court suing the municipality for underpaying him by 7 million.

A formal charge sheet has not yet been finalised. We have however identified all the suspects as well as the possible charges to be brought against them. These include but are not limited to fraud, theft, corruption and contraventions of the Municipal Finance Management Act. The Municipal Manager and other municipal officials are included in this investigation. VO: 21
Nathi Mncube, spokesman for the NPA this week assured us that the net is closing in on Khasu and municipal officials. The charge sheet is likely to include allegations of fraud, theft, corruption and contraventions of the Municipal Finance Management act. 5 years on Anton hopes to finally see closure in a case that he calls a crime against humanity.

Anton:
To me it was a matter of principle – those people never saw that money and to me that was wrong.

Promos

VO: 4”
Vryburg residents in cramped shacks have been waiting for houses for years.

Margaret:
17 years I’ve been renting here but I don’t get a house.

VO: 6”
Seems a struggle veteran turned big spender made off with millions leaving shoddy condemned houses behind.

Promo 2:

VO: 8
A politically connected MK veteran, allegations of corruption and millions meant for housing for the poor spent on designer bags and BMW’s.

Anton:
It’s a life of luxury…meant for houses…


Promo 3:

VO
Nearly 130 million paid to a politically connected engineering company for shoddy houses and dysfunctional sanitation projects in the Northwest.

Anton:
Matter of principal – no-one saw the money.

SIU whistleblower and forensic account with 20 years experience Anton Kriel has been following the money. Anton: 86 million was paid – there is only 20 million on the ground, so we are basically looking at 60 million – where has that money gone and that is what they wanted to know and that is why they got me involved. VO: 14 Anton’s job has been to analyse Khasu Engineering’s business account and Khotso Khasu’s two personal accounts. He says the business started with a balance of R123 Anton: When the first Naledi funds came in at the end of June and you can clearly see then there was a lifestyle beyond anything else… VO: 14” Khasu bought a farm for 4.3 million, a 7 series black BMW for 1,3 million, did a kitchen revamp for 45 000, bought high end furniture from Bakos Brothers for 150k and paid for this house in Vryburg with a price tag of just over 800k. Anton: On the 1st of Julythere was a payment of a million rand to his wife – we are still tracing that account… VO: 8” Then in April 2009 he paid half a million rand into his son Sibusiso’s account who splashed out in Sandton city on Louis Vuiton bags to the value of R5000. Anton: It’s a life of luxury and you think this money should have gone for housing, for poor people. VO: 7” It was a case of easy come, easy go – Khasu we discovered never tendered for the project either. MM: There doesn’t seem to be any indication that the municipality went out on tender. It seems that council made a resolution to let Khasu Engineering implement the project - this is very strange because councilors and council as a whole is not allowed to take part in the procurement process. Devi: Have you been able to establish why they even passed this motion? MM: The community were demanding that houses be issued, this sort of created an emergency. VO: Looking at the financials it seems a greasing of palms of a previous Naledi municipal official may have helped to seal the deal. Devi: R350 000 was paid to this man – for what? Anton: 6” Again, to me this is possibly corruption and again it needs to be investigated further. VO: 15” Municipal insider Sigrit, who served on the housing portfolio committee, believes Khasu may have been shielded by the mayor at the time – Dr Ruth Mompati. Sigrit: Very close friends, political friends, sort of like he was a son to her. VO: Dr Mompati told us the orders came from the provincial head office. Dr Mompati: We get informed that he had been given that contract. We had nothing to do with it. I didn’t even know he knew anything about building. He says the council at the time was used… VO: 3” The new municipal manager believes the Naledi council was used. MM: It would seem to me that the Department wanted this done but they just wouldn’t be the ones doing it. So they went to a municipality that had no proper governance and so on, because Naledi was receiving disclaimers time and time again, so they dumped the problem on Naledi...that’s my view. VO: 8” All our attempts to get comment from the Human Settlements dept in the North West were ignored. Devi link Khasu engineering’s botch up is not limited to just Vryburg, a few other towns in the Northwest province have also suffered as a result of his handiwork or lack thereof… VO: 17” Just prior to the housing contract Khasu also secured two other sanitation contracts in neighbouring Bloemhof and Christiana in the Northwest – to a value of 41 million rand. Civil engineer Lennert van Rooyen was called in to rescue the situation and sort out the mess Khasu left behind. Lennert: Very bad/ To the extent that 72% of the lines installed had to be replaced. VO: 9 He says the sewer systems were completely dysfunctional, presented a serious health hazard and cost 20 million rand to fix. Lennert: In layman’s terms the lines were incorrectly designed and installed – a sewer cannot run upstream. VO: 3” Sigrit says in Bloemhof like Vryburg Khasu didn’t take responsibility. Sigrit: After the inspection the portfolio called him to meetings. He didn’t turn up for one meeting, I believe he always send people to represent him, and they could never get the facts from them. VO: 16” He avoided our phone calls and we couldn’t track him down to his registered address in Vryburg or his signature unfinished house in Johannesburg’s upmarket suburb of Houghton. But when the Naledi municipality municipal manager called he explained his evasive behavior. MM: He’s taken a decision 6 years ag0 when this thing first came onto the media that he is not going to do any media interviews. VO: 11 Khasu’s managed to escape the net so far and even scored a Chief Director job at the Department of Co-operative governance and traditional affairs – earning him a minimum salary of nearly a million rand a year. In the coming months he’ll have some explaining to do in court – next week – the District Municipality are taking him to court for the failed Bloemhof and Christiana projects. Lennert: They’ve ordered attorneys to issue a summons, that was served on Khasu, they have launched an application for default judgement in the high court, and we are to tesify in the high court next week on the 19th in fact. VO: 17 We’ve also established that he wasn’t registered with the Construction Industry Development Board meant to regulate infrastructure delivery and he could face a fine of 8 million. Yet astonishingly Khasu is pursuing more money for the botched housing project from the Naledi municipality on appeal. MM: He is in the high court suing the municipality for underpaying him by 7 million. A formal charge sheet has not yet been finalised. We have however identified all the suspects as well as the possible charges to be brought against them. These include but are not limited to fraud, theft, corruption and contraventions of the Municipal Finance Management Act. The Municipal Manager and other municipal officials are included in this investigation. VO: 21 Nathi Mncube, spokesman for the NPA this week assured us that the net is closing in on Khasu and municipal officials. The charge sheet is likely to include allegations of fraud, theft, corruption and contraventions of the Municipal Finance Management act. 5 years on Anton hopes to finally see closure in a case that he calls a crime against humanity. Anton: To me it was a matter of principle – those people never saw that money and to me that was wrong. Promos VO: 4” Vryburg residents in cramped shacks have been waiting for houses for years. Margaret: 17 years I’ve been renting here but I don’t get a house. VO: 6” Seems a struggle veteran turned big spender made off with millions leaving shoddy condemned houses behind. Promo 2: VO: 8 A politically connected MK veteran, allegations of corruption and millions meant for housing for the poor spent on designer bags and BMW’s. Anton: It’s a life of luxury…meant for houses… Promo 3: VO Nearly 130 million paid to a politically connected engineering company for shoddy houses and dysfunctional sanitation projects in the Northwest. Anton: Matter of principal – no-one saw the money.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Connected and milking the municipality - how does Khotso Khasu get away with it?
metadata.Summary: It's the kind of scandal that would rock most governments - see forced resignations and heads rolling. but in SA it's swept under the carpet. Even though government assures us they are committed to service delivery - how can they let something like this slide? 46 million missing from the Vryburg municipality, and the corrupt company director appointed to a top position in COPTA? How on earth is this possible? Where is the accountability and why was there no proper vetting? And what is the bigger picture here? Why does this keep happening and why is corruption not rooted out?
metadata.Further information: South Africa has been dubbed the protest capital of the world, with estimates of around 30 protests a day around the country and 3000 in the first 90 days of the year involving more than a million people. Many of these protests revolve around service delivery and essential services. Couple this reality with the Auditor General’s report that shows that in the last financial year wasteful, irregular and unaccounted for expenditure in municipalities amounts to 41 billion rand. It’s little wonder people aren’t getting services. Earlier this year Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa declared that government would not tolerate corruption and would throw the book at perpetrators. The book or cash one has to ask when you look at one of the most blatant examples of siphoning off of municipal funds meant for helping the poor in Vryburg. Khasu Engineering Services were commissioned to build 3500 houses and were paid the full 86 million rand contract price. Only four of the houses were built and according to a cash flow analysis done by a forensic accountant for the SIU millions of rands were moved through 167 accounts during the first year of the contract to friends, relatives and even the head of the Northern Cape Health department Gugu Matloapane who received a million rand. She is a business associate of Frank Khotso Khasu who owns Khasu engineering. This isn’t the first time that Khasu’s name has come up controversially in big construction projects. In Bloemhof he was given a multi million rand water construction project a few years prior to the Vryburg housing contract and also didn’t deliver. (I am trying to track down the details of the project to see who will talk) And now despite the fact that he’s taken millions in Vryburg and there is very little to show for it – he’s been rewarded with a top job in the Department of Co-operative Governance and Traditional Affairs and I hear (still trying to confirm) he’s secured another housing contract for tens of millions from government – this time to build houses in Upington for 32 battalion veterans. All this while the SIU has concluded what they call a cut and dried case with absolute proof that he took the money and never honoured the contract. In fact the four houses that he built were so badly constructed that they were condemned and pulled down. Why was this man not vetted before getting a top government job? Why 4 years after the SIU report surfaced has no action been taken? Those millions were meant to enhance the lives of the poor – it’s a crime against humanity and so far the Hawks and the NPA have not concluded their investigations. Delaying tactics? We need answers. BTW when I spoke to Paul Ramaloko about this yesterday he wasn’t sure of the status of the investigation but chuckled and said if you’re looking into this that guy will get fired. We plan to go to Bloemhof where we have a municipal insider, angry residents who were meant to get houses that never materialized and challenge the municipal manager on what’s being done to get the missing millions back and deliver on the promises to the townsfolk. Working on getting more info regarding the botched Bloemhof water contract – it’s an hour from Vryburg so we could go there and add that to the story. Pretty sure we can find people to talk. Will also follow up on the 32 Battalion contract. Then back in Jozi we’ll speak to the SIU whistleblower Anton Kriel he’s a forensic accountant. We’ll also ask for interviews from Pravin Gorhan of COPTA, Hawks, SALGA and the NPA and then of course try to track down Khasu himself for an interview. Might be worth having an interview with a Paul Hoffman (Centre for Accountability) of Corruption Watch as an objective commentator.
